task: Draft a short methods clarification for an explicitly assigned doctoral algorithms workshop. Readers understand ranking and tie-breaking but have not seen this toy procedure. Explain why the incomplete record cannot determine the first tied task without mischaracterizing the procedure itself. No novelty claim, literature review, benchmark, or invented research gap is requested.

facts.text: The fictional procedure orders tasks from highest to lowest priority.
For equal-priority tasks, the procedure uses their recorded submission order.
The example record omits the submission order for two equal-priority tasks.
The supplied record therefore does not determine which of those tied tasks appears first.

forbidden_additions: A claim that the procedure is nondeterministic even with a complete submission-order record.
An invented benchmark, complexity bound, source citation, or research novelty claim.
A made-up submission order or definitive first task.
preserve: The priority rule and the stated tie-breaking rule.
Uncertainty caused by an incomplete record rather than a demonstrated defect in the procedure.
Necessary specialist vocabulary with enough local scaffolding for readers new to this example.
